title: Theme-color assertions must use theme tokens, not hardcoded hex values
answers: Why did my test break after a theme palette update?
How should I assert a component's text/background color in a test?
Test asserting '#6CCF8E' or similar hex fails after theme change
What's the convention for testing theme-dependent colors?
body:
Symptom: a passing test starts failing after an unrelated theme palette change, even though the component still uses the correct semantic color token.
Root cause: test hardcodes the current resolved hex/RGB value instead of the semantic token, e.g. `toHaveStyle({ color: '#6CCF8E' })` in packages/grafana-ui/src/components/Table/TableNG/TableNG.test.tsx.
Fix pattern: derive the expected value from the theme object passed to the component (or its provider) and assert the specific semantic token, e.g. `toHaveStyle({ color: theme.components.codeEditor.string })`; for theme-switching tests, re-assert against each supplied theme after rerendering.
Constraints: applies only to consumers of theme colors (components/styles that read tokens). Does NOT apply to tests of the color resolver, transformation function, or palette definition itself — those must keep independent frozen-literal expected values rather than calling the implementation under test to produce its own expectation.
applies: Frontend tests (grafana-ui and elsewhere) that assert element color/style derived from the theme.
says: Table panel row text color looks unreadable after updating the default theme palette.
Ensure table cell colors automatically adapt when users toggle between light and dark modes.
Code editor syntax text highlighting remains the old green after the palette refresh.
Update data grid background shades to match our newly refreshed brand color palette.
Switching themes leaves table numbers rendered in outdated colors from the previous theme.
search: Frontend test assertions for theme colors must derive expected values from the theme object, not hardcode hex/RGB literals. Hardcoded colors cause test failures after unrelated theme palette changes even when the component uses the correct semantic token. Use `toHaveStyle({ color: theme.components.codeEditor.string })` instead of `toHaveStyle({ color: '#6CCF8E' })`; for theme-switching tests, re-assert against each supplied theme after rerendering. This rule applies only to consumers of theme colors (components/styles reading tokens), NOT to tests of the color resolver, transformation function, or palette definition itself—those must keep frozen-literal expected values. Guidance in .claude/skills/frontend-testing-strategy/SKILL.md and demonstrated in packages/grafana-ui/src/components/Table/TableNG/TableNG.test.tsx.
